q: By the oath of those angels who harshly extract
(tear out the souls of the Kuffaar)...
v.s: By those [angels] who extract with violence
v.c: By those ˹angels˺ stripping out ˹evil souls˺ harshly,

q: (draw out the souls of the Mu'mineen as gently as they)
v.s: And [by] those who remove with ease
v.c: and those pulling out ˹good souls˺ gently,

q: (speedily take the souls of the dead to the heavens as if they)
v.s: And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming
v.c: and those gliding ˹through heavens˺ swiftly,

m: And those who race each other
q: (along with the souls after Allaah instructs them whether the soul should be rewarded among the righteous or punished with the Kuffaar and sinners)...
v.s: And those who race each other in a race
v.c: and those taking the lead vigorously,

v.s: And those who arrange [each] matter,
v.c: and those conducting affairs ˹obediently˺!

v.s: On the Day the blast [of the Horn] will convulse [creation],
v.c: ˹Consider˺ the Day ˹when˺ the quaking Blast will come to pass,

q: (After the first blowing of the trumpet causes everything to perish, the second blowing will bring creation back to life for reckoning.)
v.s: There will follow it the subsequent [one].
v.c: followed by a second Blast.

q: On that day, many hearts will be fluttering
v.s: Hearts, that Day, will tremble,
v.c: ˹The deniers’˺ hearts on that Day will be trembling ˹in horror˺,

q: (in embarrassment for what they did in the world and in humility before Allaah).
v.s: Their eyes humbled.
v.c: with their eyes downcast.

q: say, “Will we be returned to our former states
(will we be raised up on the Day of Qiyaamah)...”
v.s: They are [presently] saying, "Will we indeed be returned to [our] former state [of life]?
v.c: ˹But now˺ they ask ˹mockingly˺, “Will we really be restored to our former state,

v.s: Even if we should be decayed bones?"
v.c: even after we have been reduced to decayed bones?”

q: the return shall be a tremendous loss
(to us because we have not prepared).”
v.s: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."
v.c: Adding, “Then such a return would be a ˹total˺ loss ˹for us˺!”

q: It will be only a single blast
(of the trumpet to signal the arrival of Qiyaamah)...
v.s: Indeed, it will be but one shout,
v.c: But indeed, it will take only one ˹mighty˺ Blast,

q: ...and they will all immediately be awakened
(from their graves to present themselves for Reckoning).
v.s: And suddenly they will be [alert] upon the earth's surface.
v.c: and at once they will be above ground.

q: Has the story of Moosa ﵊ reached you?
v.s: Has there reached you the story of Moses? -
v.c: Has the story of Moses reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

q: When his Rabb called him in the holy valley of Tuwa
(and commanded him to take the message of Towheed to Fir'oun and his people).
v.s: When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwā,
v.c: His Lord called him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwa,

q: Fir'oun for he has certainly transgressed
v.s: "Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
v.c: ˹commanding,˺ “Go to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.

q: “Tell him, 'Do you want to be purified
v.s: And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself
v.c: And say, ‘Would you ˹be willing to˺ purify yourself,

q: ‘“And should I guide you to your Rabb so that you may fear
v.s: And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'"
v.c: and let me guide you to your Lord so that you will be in awe ˹of Him˺?’”

v.s: And he showed him the greatest sign,
v.c: Then Moses showed him the great sign,

q: (the commands of Allaah that Moosa ﵊ conveyed to him).
v.s: But he [i.e., Pharaoh] denied and disobeyed.
v.c: but he denied and disobeyed ˹Allah˺,

q: Then he turned back and applied himself
v.s: Then he turned his back, striving [i.e., plotting].
v.c: then turned his back, striving ˹against the truth˺.

v.s: And he gathered [his people] and called out.
v.c: Then he summoned ˹his people˺ and called out,

v.s: And said, "I am your most exalted lord."
v.c: saying, “I am your lord, the most high!”

q: Allaah seized him with the punishment of this world
v.s: So God seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression]..
v.c: So Allah overtook him, making him an example in this life and the next.

q: in this for the one who fears
v.s: Indeed in that is a lesson [i.e., warning] for whoever would fear [God].
v.c: Surely in this is a lesson for whoever stands in awe of ˹Allah˺.

q: more difficult to create or the sky
(which is much larger)? (If Allaah could create something as immense and magnificent as the sky, resurrecting mankind on the Day of Qiyaamah is extremely easy for Him.)
v.s: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? He [i.e., God] constructed it.
v.c: Which is harder to create: you or the sky? He built it,

v.s: He raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
v.c: raising it high and forming it flawlessly.

q: ...made its night dark and made its light manifest
(by) the rising and setting of the sun).
v.s: And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.
v.c: He dimmed its night, and brought forth its daylight.

v.s: And after that He spread the earth.
v.c: As for the earth, He spread it out as well,

q: from the earth her water and fodder
v.s: He extracted from it its water and its pasture,
v.c: bringing forth its water and pastures

v.s: And the mountains He set firmly
v.c: and setting the mountains firmly ˹upon it˺—

q: and for the benefit of your animals
(so that you all can have food to eat and water to drink).
v.s: As enjoyment [i.e., provision] for you and your grazing livestock.
v.c: all as ˹a means of˺ sustenance for you and your animals.

v.s: But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity -
v.c: But, when the Supreme Disaster comes to pass—

v.s: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove,
v.c: the Day every person will remember all ˹their˺ striving,

q: ...and Jahannam will be clearly visible to those who look on.
v.s: And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see -
v.c: and the Hellfire will be displayed for all to see—

q: As for the one who transgresses
v.s: So as for he who transgressed
v.c: then as for those who transgressed

q: ...and who prefers the life of this world
v.s: And preferred the life of the world,
v.c: and preferred the ˹fleeting˺ life of this world,

q: ...then Jahannam shall certainly be his abode
v.s: Then indeed, Hellfire will be [his] refuge.
v.c: the Hellfire will certainly be ˹their˺ home.

q: As for the one who fears standing
before his Rabb and who restrains himself from carnal passions
v.s: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,
v.c: And as for those who were in awe of standing before their Lord and restrained themselves from ˹evil˺ desires,

q: ...then Jannah shall definitely be his abode.
v.s: Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.
v.c: Paradise will certainly be ˹their˺ home.

q: about when Qiyaamah will take place.
v.s: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?
v.c: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the Hour, “When will it be?”

q: What have you to tell about it
(when) you have no knowledge about when it will occur)?
v.s: In what [position] are you that you should mention it?
v.c: But it is not for you to tell its time.

q: (Only Allaah knows when Qiyaamah will take place.)
v.s: To your Lord is its finality.
v.c: That knowledge rests with your Lord ˹alone˺.

q: are a Warner only to him who fears it
v.s: You are only a warner for those who fear it.
v.c: Your duty is only to warn whoever is in awe of it.

q: The day when they see it
(tarried in this world and in the grave for)
only an evening or a morning
(compared to Qiyaamah which will be so long and dreadful).
v.s: It will be, on the Day they see it, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.
v.c: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had stayed ˹in the world˺ no more than one evening or its morning.
